title: The Central Pawn and Freedom of Manoeuvre
subtitle: A supplementary diagram from the Ruy Lopez discussion

source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter VI, §32 Some Possible Developments from a Ruy Lopez, supplementary final diagram under Example 65

narration.say: This lesson continues the strategic discussion in Example 65. The supplied TeX does not contain a separate Example 66 heading.
Capablanca gives this diagram without the moves leading to it. Black is to move. The white king has joined the attack.
The advanced e-pawn controls d6 and f6. Its potential advance after exchanges is the pivot of White’s plan.
White’s major pieces have room to manoeuvre. Black must watch the pressure along the c-file and the kingside pawn structure.

steps.title: A rook move meets the immediate pressure

narration.say: In the book’s analysis, Black must bring the rook to f8.

exercise.prompt: Follow the book: move Black’s rook from d8 to f8.

feedback.*: The rook on d8 moves to f8.

exercise.hint: The rook on d8 moves to f8.

steps.title: The king is part of the attack

narration.say: White has moved the queen to c2. Capablanca’s next idea is to bring the king to f3 and increase the pressure on the pawn formation.
The book does not specify Black’s intervening reply. We therefore explain the plan without inventing another move sequence.
The diagram is an exercise in strategic imagination. Ask what the exchanges would leave behind and which pieces have freedom to act.
White’s central pawn, active king and mobile major pieces belong to one coherent plan.
